tasks.blocked_on: Commando.sng is the project's ONLY byte-exact fidelity anchor and 26 tests assert against it. Commando's voice 1 plays the wrong octave on 96 of its 237 voice-1 attacks (141 are already exact), and ANY fix necessarily changes Commando.sng and breaks those tests. THE QUESTION: may Commando.sng be re-cut when a fix is found -- and if so, against what (a new hand-verified reference, or simply the new output)? A 'no' is a good answer and closes the pitch task as won't-fix with a reason. ================ UPDATE AT bd28b6a: THE DIAGNOSIS IS COMPLETE, so this is now a clean yes/no rather than a question asked against an unknown. The mechanism is settled: note byte $68 = 104 overruns the player's 96-entry frequency table, and the player reads $54F8/$54F9 -- voices 0 and 1 STORED WAVEFORM bytes -- as the frequency. Instruments carrying $41 reduce to entry 71 and the one carrying $21 to entry 59, which is exactly the original's measured 95/1 split. We clamp every note byte >= 92 to GT_LASTNOTE (`patterns.py:495`), so voice 1 plays G#7 on 110 events. WHAT A FIX WOULD COST: reproducing the original means emitting a fixed very high pitch (entry 71 for a $41 instrument) rather than a clamp to 92 -- a 21-semitone move on 110 of voice 1's notes -- and Commando.sng is the project's ONLY byte-exact anchor, asserted by 26 tests. THE QUESTION IS UNCHANGED: may Commando.sng be re-cut and those tests re-based? Note the honest counter-argument, which did not exist before the diagnosis: what the original sounds there is not a musical note at all, it is whatever two waveform registers happen to hold, so 'faithful' and 'better' may not be the same answer here and a listen should probably decide it.
